summary: 80-foot steel lookout on McGarr Ridge, Ozark County, MO; built 1936-37 and CCC-manned in 1937; no later record in the sources read.

staffing.status: manned by the CCC Hammond Mill crew in February 1937; local men employed to man it by March 1937

facts.agency: Mark Twain National Forest (White River Ranger District, per 1937 reports)

events.note: Work progressing on a new 80-foot steel tower about a mile southwest of the Hammond Mill CCC camp (report dated December 17, 1936)
Completed on McGarr Ridge by February 25, 1937 (report dated February 25, 1937)
Being manned by the CCC Hammond Mill boys after completion (report dated February 25, 1937)
Local men employed to man the Siloam Springs and Dogtown towers, reported after a February 23-25 fire training school at Camp F-6 (report dated March 4, 1937)

evidence.supports: 80-foot steel tower being erected about a mile southwest of the Hammond Mill CCC camp, December 1936
evidence.quote: Work is progressing rapidly on the new 80-foot steel tower being erected a mile southwest of the Hammond Mill CCC Camp.

evidence.supports: tower counted as one of four on the Spring Creek and White River ranger districts
evidence.quote: making a total of four towers on the Spring Creek and White River Ranger districts

evidence.supports: tower expected to help spot and locate fires
evidence.quote: will aid materially in spotting and accurately locating fires

evidence.supports: completed towers in the group had living quarters and a garage on the ground for a full-time lookout guard
evidence.quote: The completed towers include living quarters and garage on the ground, constructed for the purpose of housing a full time lookout guard.

evidence.supports: tower on McGarr Ridge in the south part of the White River Ranger District
evidence.quote: located on McGarr Ridge in the south part of the White River Ranger District

evidence.supports: tower completed and being manned by the CCC Hammond Mill boys, February 1937
evidence.quote: has been completed and is now being manned by the CCC Hammond Mill boys

evidence.supports: temporary telephone line in use while the permanent line was under construction
evidence.quote: A temporary telephone line is being used at present, pending the completion of the permanent line which is under construction.

evidence.supports: expected fires in that portion of the district to be more readily detected, with crews dispatched to the fire
evidence.quote: It is expected that by the use of this structure fires in that portion of the district may be more readily detected and crews dispatched to the fire.

evidence.quote: Missouri Lookouts - Ozark County - Mark Twain National Forest

evidence.supports: three-day fire training school at Camp F-6, February 23-25, 1937
evidence.quote: held a three-day Fire Training School at Camp F-6 on Feb. 23, 24, and 25

evidence.quote: local men employed to man the Siloam Springs and Dogtown Lookout Towers

notes_for_editor: One source only: the Central US Lookouts page, which quotes 1936-37 Howell County Gazette items. Nothing after 1937 was found, so status, access and visit are left out rather than guessed; the brief's status 'unknown' should stay until a source confirms it. Two WebSearch queries and the inventory pages turned up nothing on Dogtown. livingnewdeal.org and missourilife.com returned 403, ebandflo.org did not resolve, and firetower.org lists only two former Missouri sites (Grassy, Gypsy), neither of them Dogtown. Possible next checks: Mark Twain National Forest records for McGarr Ridge, and Bob Frakes, A Place Above the Trees. The brief's county, agency and 24.4 m height agree with the page, so no corrections are proposed.
